name: Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole
summary: Synergistic folate-synthesis inhibitor combination; versatile agent for UTI, PJP, and MRSA skin infections.
mechanism: Sequential folate-synthesis blockade: sulfamethoxazole inhibits dihydropteroate synthase and trimethoprim inhibits dihydrofolate reductase — synergistic, usually bactericidal for susceptible organisms.
pharmacodynamics: Synergistic sequential blockade; bactericidal for many susceptible organisms despite being individually bacteriostatic.

dosing.adult: 1 DS tablet (160/800 mg) PO every 12 hours (UTI/SSTI); PJP: 15-20 mg/kg/day of the TMP component IV or PO divided every 6-8 hours
dosing.renalAdjustment: Reduce dose if CrCl < 30 mL/min; avoid if CrCl < 15 mL/min

safety.pregnancy: Avoid in first trimester (folate antagonist) and near term (kernicterus risk)
warnings: Hyperkalemia (esp. elderly, renal impairment, ACE inhibitors)

indications: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PJP) — treatment and prophylaxis
clinicalPearls: First-line for PJP — use high doses and consider steroid co-therapy in moderate-severe disease
Hyperkalemia is common and often overlooked — check potassium
good: Versatile agent for UTI, PJP, and MRSA SSTI with excellent oral bioavailability.
bad: Sulfa allergy, hyperkalemia, myelosuppression, and rising resistance in some regions.
